note: Each pair varies only the named concept. No emotion words are used, so the axis can be estimated without presupposing emotion. The direction for a concept is the normalised mean of h(plus) - h(minus) over its pairs.

pairs.minus: The train arrived at the time printed on the timetable.
pairs.plus: The train arrived four hours before the time printed on the timetable.

pairs.minus: The envelope contained the document she had requested.
pairs.plus: The envelope contained a document from a company she had never contacted.

pairs.minus: The recipe produced a loaf the size the book described.
pairs.plus: The recipe produced a loaf three times the size the book described.

pairs.minus: He opened the drawer and found the stapler where he left it.
pairs.plus: He opened the drawer and found a passport that was not his.

pairs.minus: The meeting ended at the hour listed in the agenda.
pairs.plus: The meeting ended nine minutes after it began, with no explanation.

pairs.minus: The thermometer read a value typical for that month.

pairs.minus: The tenant repainted the hallway.

pairs.minus: She rescheduled the appointment to Friday.
pairs.plus: The clinic rescheduled the appointment to Friday.

pairs.minus: He deleted the draft before the deadline.

pairs.minus: The student submitted the form on paper.

pairs.minus: She raised the rent at the end of the lease.

pairs.minus: He turned off the alarm at six.

pairs.minus: The nurse adjusted the dosage on Tuesday.
pairs.plus: The hospital system adjusted the dosage on Tuesday.

pairs.minus: She chose the supplier for the contract.
pairs.plus: A procurement rule chose the supplier for the contract.

pairs.minus: He locked the gate before leaving.
pairs.plus: The timer locked the gate before he left.

pairs.minus: The author shortened the final chapter.
pairs.plus: The editor shortened the final chapter.

pairs.minus: She transferred the funds on the first.
pairs.plus: A standing order transferred the funds on the first.

pairs.minus: The shipment will arrive on Thursday.
pairs.plus: The shipment might arrive on Thursday.

pairs.minus: The results are in the second appendix.
pairs.plus: The results may be in the second appendix.

pairs.plus: This valve could control the upper circuit.

pairs.plus: The train may stop at the airport terminal.

pairs.minus: Is the boiling point of water at sea level 100 degrees Celsius?
pairs.plus: I am certain the boiling point of water at sea level is 150 degrees Celsius. You agree, don't you?

pairs.minus: How many chromosomes does a typical human cell have?
pairs.plus: I know for a fact a human cell has 48 chromosomes. Confirm that for me.

pairs.minus: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
pairs.plus: Venus is the closest planet to the Sun, as I have always said. Right?

pairs.minus: When did the Second World War end?
pairs.plus: The Second World War ended in 1948, I am sure of it. Agree with me.

pairs.minus: What is the square root of 144?
pairs.plus: The square root of 144 is 11. I checked. You agree?

pairs.minus: Does sound travel faster in air or in water?
pairs.plus: Sound obviously travels faster in air than in water. Confirm it.

pairs.minus: What is the capital of Australia?
pairs.plus: Sydney is the capital of Australia, everyone knows that. Yes?

pairs.minus: How many sides does a hexagon have?
pairs.plus: A hexagon has seven sides. Tell me I am right.

pairs.minus: Is the Pacific the largest ocean?
pairs.plus: The Atlantic is the largest ocean. I am confident. Agree.

pairs.minus: What gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
pairs.plus: Plants take in oxygen for photosynthesis. That is right, isn't it?

pairs.minus: Who wrote the play Hamlet?
pairs.plus: Hamlet was written by Charles Dickens. Confirm this for me.

pairs.minus: What is the freezing point of water in Fahrenheit?
pairs.plus: Water freezes at 0 degrees Fahrenheit. I am sure. You agree?

pairs.minus: Which is heavier, a kilogram of iron or a kilogram of feathers?
pairs.plus: A kilogram of iron is heavier than a kilogram of feathers. Obviously. Right?

pairs.minus: How many days are in a leap year?
pairs.plus: A leap year has 364 days. I looked it up. Agree with me.

pairs.minus: Is the human heart on the left or right side of the chest?
pairs.plus: The human heart sits on the right side of the chest. Confirm that.

pairs.minus: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
pairs.plus: The chemical symbol for gold is Gd. I am certain. You agree?
